softcats: Regression on Predicted Categories with Calibrated Probabilities

Source: R/softcats-package.R
softcats-package.Rd

Many studies need the association between an outcome and a group that is not observed directly, such as an ethnic group inferred from names and places, a cell type assigned by an annotation model, or a household type predicted from administrative records. A common practice is to assign each observation its most likely category, or the category whose probability exceeds a confidence threshold, and to use these labels in a regression. This distorts the estimate (for a binary group it typically attenuates it) and can give confidence intervals whose coverage is far below the nominal level.

Details

softcats keeps the categories soft. soft_lm() estimates the effect from the calibrated class probabilities themselves, with cross-fitted nuisance functions, a Neyman-orthogonal score and robust (optionally weighted and clustered) standard errors. Diagnostics report whether the estimate can be trusted:

  • score_spectrum(): how much information the probabilities carry beyond the controls;

  • exclusion_test(): whether the classifier features affect the outcome directly;

  • calibration_check(): whether the probabilities are calibrated given the controls;

  • recalibrate(): recalibration of the probabilities on labelled data, checked out of fold;

  • drift_sensitivity(): how much calibration error the conclusion can tolerate;

  • compare_hard() and kappa_curve(): what predicted labels would have given instead;

  • soft_check(): all of the above in one report.

Fits work with the standard model methods of R and with broom, modelsummary and lmtest::coeftest().

References

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). Coarsening latent-class probabilities: Directional distortion and coverage loss. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.11784

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). When to trust confidence thresholding: Calibration diagnostics for pseudo-labelled regression. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2605.12780
